topics.topic: Ownership of liveness and readiness capabilities and HealthStatus production
questions: Which named capabilities handle liveness and readiness, and which module catches the readiness storage failure and produces its HTTP response?
Which named runtime capabilities or handlers own the liveness and readiness operations and their `HealthStatus` production?

quotes: liveness_endpoint: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST return only HealthStatus(status='ok') to prove the process can answer and MUST NOT expose paths, credentials, schema details, dependency versions, configuration, or exception text.

readiness_endpoint: [BEHAVIOR] MUST perform the bounded storage initialization check by opening one transaction with store.begin(), which returns a PortalTransaction and creates any missing schemas (storage initialization, not product state: no product row is written), and closing it with exactly one tx.rollback(), rolling back on failure only while it is still open, return only the generic health response, exposing no path, credential, schema, dependency version, configuration or exception detail, and MUST NOT mutate product state.

A store or application construction failure propagates. Readiness opens and
closes one portal transaction; when that cannot be opened it answers 500
with no `HealthStatus` body and no internal detail, never `ok`. Liveness does
not touch the store.
judgement.why: The later runtime notes name both endpoint operations, assign their HealthStatus behavior to runtime, and specify the concealed HTTP 500 readiness failure.

topics.topic: Readiness success criterion across database opening, schema creation, and rollback
questions: Does readiness report `ok` merely when the database connection opens, or only after every create-on-begin schema operation also succeeds?
Does readiness report ok merely when the database connection opens, or only after PortalStore.begin completes all schema creation successfully and the transaction rolls back successfully?

judgement.why: P3 judged the same readiness success criterion on the same passages, and the reopening change has not altered it.

precedent.topic: Readiness success criterion for database initialization
quotes: readiness_endpoint: [BEHAVIOR] MUST perform the bounded storage initialization check by opening one transaction with store.begin(), which returns a PortalTransaction and creates any missing schemas (storage initialization, not product state: no product row is written), and closing it with exactly one tx.rollback(), rolling back on failure only while it is still open, return only the generic health response, exposing no path, credential, schema, dependency version, configuration or exception detail, and MUST NOT mutate product state.

PortalStore.begin: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST open exactly one SQLite connection for the supplied database_url, call create_audit_schema, create_project_tracking_schema, create_project_section_schema, create_budget_schema, create_snapshot_import_schema, create_expense_schema, create_progress_photo_schema, create_staff_access_schema, create_client_access_schema, and create_producer_identity_schema on that same connection, and return a new open PortalTransaction owning it; a failure MUST close the new connection and raise PersistenceError, and no active transaction may be shared implicitly. The connection installs no row factory, so every query returns a positional tuple row and a repository decodes a column by its position in the table's declared column order; reading a column by name raises TypeError against this connection and MUST NOT be emitted.
precedent.why: The later notes require readiness to complete `store.begin`, including every schema-creation call, so a schema-creation failure prevents the ready response.

topics.topic: HTTP response when readiness encounters a storage failure
questions: What observable health response is returned when readiness encounters the storage failure?

judgement.why: P2 judged the same readiness storage-failure response question on the same texts, and the reopening change has not altered it.

precedent.topic: Readiness failure HTTP status and response body
quotes:
A store or application construction failure propagates. Readiness opens and
closes one portal transaction; when that cannot be opened it answers 500
with no `HealthStatus` body and no internal detail, never `ok`. Liveness does
not touch the store.

readiness_endpoint: [BEHAVIOR] MUST perform the bounded storage initialization check by opening one transaction with store.begin(), which returns a PortalTransaction and creates any missing schemas (storage initialization, not product state: no product row is written), and closing it with exactly one tx.rollback(), rolling back on failure only while it is still open, return only the generic health response, exposing no path, credential, schema, dependency version, configuration or exception detail, and MUST NOT mutate product state.
precedent.why: State 5 specifies that failure to open the readiness transaction, including its schema initialization, returns HTTP 500 with no HealthStatus body or internal detail, while the later note fixes the rollback behavior.

topics.topic: HTTP server startup, application binding, and ownership
questions: What operation starts the HTTP server and binds the runtime application, and which module or external deployment component owns it?

quotes:
### Callers

`boundary:deployment_process`.

### Inputs

`RuntimeSettings` supplied by the caller.

### Outputs

The outer FastAPI application.
judgement.why: State 5 makes create_runtime_app an application factory called by the deployment boundary and returning the outer FastAPI application, leaving server execution and socket binding with that external deployment boundary.

topics.topic: Required inner application mount paths after proxy prefix stripping
questions: After the proxy strips the public /api prefix, must the service expose the inner API only at its root, or must it also expose a second /api-mounted copy that makes externally double-prefixed routes reachable?

quotes:
The
inner application answers at both prefixes, so a route is reached whether
or not the proxy has stripped `/api`; behind the stripping proxy a path that
repeats the prefix (`/api/api/…`) reaches the same route, and no route
exists only under one prefix.
judgement.why: State 5 explicitly requires both mounts and makes the externally double-prefixed route reachable after one proxy prefix is stripped.

topics.topic: Runtime capture versus per-read lookup of binary environment settings
questions: Are `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` and `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` captured in RuntimeSettings at startup or reread from the environment for every binary read?

judgement.why: P7 judged the same startup-capture versus per-read environment lookup question on the unchanged binary-storage passage.

precedent.topic: Whether binary-storage environment settings are fixed at startup or reread per request
quotes:
Environment values are read once, by `runtime_settings`,
  into `RuntimeSettings`; other modules read `config.*` constants or the
  settings they are handed, never the environment, with two exceptions
  kept from the running service: `registry_gateway` reads
  `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` at each Registry call (A6, A30) and `binary_storage`
  reads `BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT` and `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` at each binary
  read, each refusing that call when its value is missing or unusable
  (Factory code `adapters/registry_gateway.py` `_registry_url`,
  `adapters/binary_storage.py`; owner 2026-11-06: current service
  behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated).
precedent.why: The unchanged passage already states that runtime settings are initially loaded once but binary_storage is a named exception that rereads and validates both binary environment values on every read, and the reopening change did not touch or affect that behavior.
